newsitem.title: USA: Access Health sees '97 EPS below forecast.
newsitem.headline: Access Health sees '97 EPS below forecast.

text.p: Access Health Inc said that while it excects second quarter earnings to be in line with analyst forecasts of $0.22 per share, full year fiscal 1997 earnings should be $0.15 to $0.17 below the consensus estimate of $0.99 per share.
It cited slower than anticipated revenue growth for the shortfall.
The company also said it expects second quarter revenues to be slightly above the first quarter level. In that period, Access reported total revenues of about $13.8 million.
Revenue for fiscal 1997 will be about 10 to 15 percent below analyst expectations, the company said.

It said sales were hurt by slower net enrollment growth due to a lengthening of sales cycles, slower roll-out of Access Health services by new customers to their members, and a decision by BlueCross BlueShield of Tennessee to discontinue Personal Health Advisor services to some of its Medicaid population. Access also cited a competitive pricing environment for its core products.

"Although we are disappointed that our near term growth rate is slower than anticipated, we are pleased that we continue to grow at a strong rate in the absolute and to win most of the competitions for major new personal health and care management contracts," Chief Executive Officer Thomas Gardner said in a statement.
The company said it expects earnings and revenues to grow by more than 35 percent in fiscal 1998.
